answer: In an agent-run harbor market, even during a gale, bots selling opal must lock a $100 bond for 30 days before receiving any buyer credit. Each account's unpaid orders are capped at its bond, which escrow uses to cover non-delivery. Creating a thousand fake sellers therefore locks $100,000 without increasing unsecured buying power: the attacker must fund every identity and bear the capital cost throughout the lockup.
